Yosemite: June 2026

The plan

Four hikes, alternating hard days with easier ones. The main thing is getting through the Arch Rock gate by 7:30 am, since parking fills up fast in summer. Route maps below are rough sketches, so use the NPS map or offline AllTrails on the trail.

Your week beats the Mon–Thu Mist Trail repair closures (those start June 30). The JMT "Ice Cut" IS closed daily, see the descent note below.
The Mist steps, what Tuesday looks like
Vernal Fall from the granite staircase, June flow. Rain shells on before this section.
  • 5:30 AMAlarm. 6:15 leave the house.
  • 7:30 AMPark at Curry Village day lot; walk or shuttle to Happy Isles trailhead.
  • 8:00–1:30Up the Mist Trail (shells on), lunch on the granite slabs at the top of Nevada Fall. Descent, per the June 2026 closure map: the JMT "Ice Cut" is closed daily through mid-July, so come down the upper Mist Trail to the Clark Point cutoff, then the JMT switchbacks the rest of the way; you still get the Nevada Fall + Liberty Cap view from Clark Point.
  • 2:00 PMDrinks at the Mountain Room Bar, Yosemite Valley Lodge. Slow afternoon: El Capitan Meadow (binoculars for climbers), Valley View pullout.
  • ~6:00 PMDinner (optional): early sitting at the Mountain Room before sunset, or just snack now and eat back at the Airbnb after.
  • 8:15 PMSunset · Sentinel Bridge / Cook's Meadow
    Half Dome alpenglow reflected in the Merced: the Ansel Adams angle. Drive home after; in bed by ten.

Note the marked water source: Yosemite Creek above the falls is the only refill on the route (filter or treat). Carry 3L each regardless.
The view from the rim
Upper Yosemite Fall from the rim, Half Dome beyond, the reward for the switchbacks.
  • 5:45 AMLeave the house, earliest Valley start of the week. 7:00 park near Camp 4 (fills very early).
  • 7:15–3:30Grind the switchbacks in morning shade. Detour to the Upper Yosemite Fall overlook, where you stand at the lip. Then 2.9 quiet miles to Eagle Peak; long summit lunch 3,500 ft above the Valley floor. Return the same way. Refill option: Yosemite Creek above the falls (filter/treat), otherwise it's a dry route.
  • 4:00 PMCool your feet in the Merced at Sentinel Beach. Optional audible: Yosemite Point (+1.6 mi from the falls junction) instead of Eagle Peak for Lost Arrow Spire close-ups.
  • EVEEasy dinner at the house. Rest night, no sunset mission. Ice cream at Happy Burger Diner if anyone's still standing.

That speck at the railing is a person. El Capitan across the void, bring the wide lens.
  • 7:30 AMLeave the house. ~9:15 parked at Glacier Point, which beats the lot jam. If full, use the Sentinel Dome/Taft Point trailhead lot 2 mi back and run the loop from there.
  • 9:30–1:00Glacier Point overlook in morning light → Sentinel Dome (360°: Half Dome, El Cap and Yosemite Falls at once) → rim trail to Taft Point → back to the car.

    It's directly on the drive home (Glacier Point Rd → Chinquapin → Wawona Rd). Adds ~15 min; home by ~9:30 with the 5:30 alarm intact.
  • NIGHTGas up in Mariposa: tomorrow is the long run and there's no fuel in the Valley.

Default, moderate

Leave mid/late afternoon, Tunnel View at golden hour en route, dinner, full sleep before Clouds Rest.

Full send, game-time call

Stay for sunset at Glacier Point itself, the best in the park, and the car's already there. Cost: home ~10 pm before the earliest alarm of the week. Only if the group is running hot.

Route map: Tenaya Lake to the summitNPS Tioga Road ↗
12.7 mi · ~4,860 ft of total up-and-down (the route dips before it climbs) · "5 hrs 45" is fast-hiker book time; budget 7+ with summit lunch. Olmsted Point on the map = your sunset stop.
The summit view
Looking DOWN on Half Dome, the whole Valley running to the horizon. This is why Friday exists.
  • 5:30 AMLeave the house: Hwy 140 → Big Oak Flat Rd → Crane Flat → Tioga Rd east. ~7:45 at Sunrise Lakes Trailhead, Tenaya Lake.
  • 7:45–3:00Steep first 1,000 ft, rolling high country, then the famous granite spine to the summit. Narrow ridge but non-technical; slow and steady. It's near 10,000 ft: pace the climb, pack layers.
  • 3:30 PMVictory feet-dunk at Tenaya Lake's beach (briefly, it's cold). Optional 20-min detour into Tuolumne Meadows.
  • ~7:30 PMSunset · Olmsted Point
    On the drive home, facing the evening light, with Half Dome from behind at golden hour. Late arrival home is fine; only departure remains.
  • 9 PM+Final-night toast: 1850 in Mariposa (optional, if back in time and anyone has the energy), otherwise dinner at the Airbnb.

Driving summary

Roughly 15–16 hours total across the week; Friday alone is nearly a third of it, which is the price of Clouds Rest from a Mariposa base. Worth it. Hwy 140 along the Merced canyon is the daily commute; watch for the occasional single-lane control near El Portal and for deer after dark.

Standing rules

Beat the gate

Through Arch Rock by ~7:30 am on Valley days. No reservation system in 2026 means fuller lots and longer lines, early is everything.

Water & layers

2–3L per person every day; 3L+ for Eagle Peak. Layers for Clouds Rest, since the summit sits near 10,000 ft and Glacier Point drops fast after sundown.

Check conditions nightly

nps.gov/yose the evening before each hike: trail notices, road work on 140, and any change to the JMT Ice Cut closure (closed daily through mid-July per the June 2026 map).

Bear-safe food

Nothing edible or scented visible in the parked car. Use the trailhead lockers where provided.

Fuel discipline

No gas in Yosemite Valley. Top up in Mariposa, especially Thursday night before the Tioga run. (Crane Flat has in-park gas at in-park prices.)

Offline everything

Save the digital pass for offline use; screenshot maps and this page. Cell service dies in the canyon and inside most of the park.

Before Monday

0 of 0 done
  • Non-Resident Annual Pass on Recreation.gov: $250, one pass covers the car (passholder + 3 adults); required since Jan 2026 to avoid the $100/person nonresident surcharge. Passholder must be present with photo ID
  • Trekking poles packed (knees will thank you on every descent)
  • Rain shells for the Mist Trail; warm layers for Clouds Rest and any sunset stop
  • Headlamps, insurance, not plans
  • Offline maps downloaded (AllTrails / Gaia / NPS app) for all four routes
  • Dinners: stock up at Pioneer Market on Monday. Optional nights out if the mood strikes: Mountain Room in the Valley (Tue, early sitting before the Sentinel Bridge sunset) or 1850 in Mariposa (Tue/Fri)
